issues: List/numbering marker case mismatch: original uses "C. Mengingat:" but translation has "C. In view of:"; downstream splitting may be case-sensitive and expects the same marker form.
Meaning drift: "Penanggulangan Pekerjaan Anak" is translated as "Handling of Child Labor"; more accurate is "Countermeasures/Control of Child Labor" (penanggulangan = countermeasures/mitigation).

List/numbering marker case mismatch: original uses "C. Mengingat:" but translation has "C. In view of:"; list marker should match exactly ("C.") and be consistently represented (use "C." not "c." or a heading).

Meaning drift in the last clause: "Dengan Persetujuan Bersama" is rendered as "With Mutual Approval"; in this legal context it should be "With Joint Approval" (i.e., joint approval of DPRD and Regent).

Scrambled/merged list numbering: several items are run together on the same line, causing markers (2), (4), 15, 16, 18 to not appear as separate list items in order (e.g., Article 1 items 1-2, 14-18; Article 5 paragraph (4); Article 6 paragraph (4); Article 7 paragraph (2)).

Markdown/list structure not preserved: original has distinct numbered items/paragraphs that must be separated; translation keeps stray standalone word "Implementation" but it is acceptable as it matches the original "Penyelenggaraan" line.
Scrambled list/numbering structure in Article 8: item (5) is embedded within item 4 and not presented as its own numbered item, causing a missing/reordered list marker.

Broken list/numbering structure in Article 8: original has item 4 containing the text for item (5) inline; translation splits them into separate items 4 and 5, changing the marker sequence/boundaries used for downstream splitting.

Meaning drift/omission: original Article 8 item 4 refers to 'Women and Children.' (with punctuation) and then continues with 'Victims of Violence' and includes the economic protection clause as marker (5) within item 4; translation does not reflect this combined structure.
